<reflection>
- The high catalyst experiment (Exp 2) successfully broke the degeneracy. Models with non-linear catalyst dependencies (M2, M8, M3) now fit significantly better than the simple linear model (M1) and the deactivation models (M11, M12, M13).
- M2 and M8 suggest a sub-linear dependence on total catalyst (monomer is active, but forms off-cycle dimers or pre-equilibria at high concentrations). M3 suggests a super-linear dependence (dimer is the active species).
- My aim for this turn is to definitively separate the monomer-active models (M2, M8) from the dimer-active model (M3), and to test the irreversible activation model (M6).
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
To distinguish between monomer-active (M2, M8) and dimer-active (M3) mechanisms, we need to probe the opposite end of the catalyst concentration spectrum. By using a very low catalyst concentration while keeping the substrate concentration identical to Exp 2, we can directly observe the reaction order with respect to the catalyst.
I propose an experiment with a low catalyst concentration (cat = 0.01) and a moderate substrate concentration (S = 2.0). 
Contrastive predictions:
- M3 (dimer active): The concentration of the active `cat2` species scales quadratically with total catalyst. Dropping [cat] by a factor of 20 (from 0.20 to 0.01) will drop the active catalyst by a factor of ~400, resulting in an almost completely flat, near-zero reaction rate.
- M2 & M8 (monomer active): At low concentrations, the catalyst exists almost entirely in its active monomeric state. The rate will scale linearly in this regime (dropping by a factor of ~20 compared to the linear expectation, but showing a much higher relative rate than M3).
- M6 (irreversible activation, cat => cat*): With a very low initial catalyst concentration, the absolute rate of activation is extremely slow. This will manifest as a pronounced lag phase (concave-up product curve) before the steady-state rate is achieved.
- M1 (simple MM): Will show standard linear scaling (exactly 1/20th the rate of Exp 2, whereas M2/M8 will be slightly faster than 1/20th because they were penalized by off-cycle species at high [cat]).
</hypothesis>
